events.title: Coffee & Colors Sunrise Cruise
events.description: Experience a fall morning on Lake Superior aboard Vista Fleet’s Coffee & Colors Cruise! Hop aboard the Vista Queen in time to catch Duluth’s iconic sunrise from the water, then take in the vibrant fall colors along the Northland’s hillsides. Along the way, learn about the Duluth-Superior Harbor, local history, the science and ecology of the St. Louis River system, and the area’s unique and historic bridges. Complimentary coffee and breakfast pastries are included, making this the perfect way to start a crisp fall day in Duluth. This cruise features open seating. Please note that the Vista Queen is not wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Whoopsa Daisy Farm
events.description: Come and explore the farm with your family. Jump in the corn pit, dig in the sandbox, or explore Dinoland and Fairyland. There are two playgrounds, yard games, a wagon ride through the Whimsical Woods and so much more. Feed the donkeys, goats, and chickens and walk through the berries. The farm is open to everyone Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, August 7 through October 25, 2026, from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm. We will also open Thursday, October 15 for MEA weekend from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm. Tickets are sold at the entrance in the yellow building. The cost is $8.00 a person, and infants are free. Everything on the farm is included in the price. We are off Highway 53 in Duluth at 5399 Samuelson Road.

events.title: Duluth River Train Excursion
events.description: Ride the Lake Superior and Mississippi Railroad. A historic 2-hour rail journey through the majestic St. Louis River Estuary. Family-friendly, volunteer-run, and purely Duluth. Our narrated tour takes you along the original Lake Superior & Mississippi line in vintage coaches. Go where cars and hiking boots can’t reach. The St. Louis River Estuary is a hidden sanctuary for bald eagles, osprey, and Northland wildlife. Bring your camera for unparalleled views of the Duluth riverfront. Best to arrive about a half-hour before departure. Our ticket office is located just off of Grand Avenue.

events.title: BoB-a-Q Smokehouse & Grill
events.description: BoB-a-Q Smokehouse & Grill is bringing bold, competition-grade barbecue to Castle Danger Brewery in 2026. Known as one of the North Shore’s premier food trucks, BoB-a-Q serves fall-off-the-bone baby back ribs, smoky-sweet brisket sandwiches, slow-cooked pulled pork, and rotating specialty items that keep fans coming back for more. With over a decade of BBQ expertise, BoB-a-Q builds every dish over wood-fired smokers, crafting fresh, made-to-order plates that are rich, flavorful, and unmistakably authentic. Whether you’re pairing a Castle Danger pint with a rack of ribs or grabbing a brisket sandwich their menu brings the perfect blend of tradition, technique, and North Shore character. We’re thrilled to welcome BoB-a-Q Smokehouse & Grill back to the taproom for another season of great food, great beer, and great community. Come hungry—their barbecue is the real deal. Check out their menu Follow them: Website: bobaqsmokehouse.com Facebook: @bobaqsmoke Instagram: @bob_a_q_smoke

events.title: Lunch & Leaves Cruise on the Vista Fleet
events.description: Experience fall in Duluth from the water aboard Vista Fleet’s Lunch & Leaves Cruise! Take in the beautiful fall colors of the Northland while enjoying a relaxing cruise aboard the Vista Star and a delicious lunch from MidCoast Catering. Choose from a Turkey, Bacon & Swiss sandwich with cranberry mayo, lettuce and tomato; a Ham & Provolone Croissant with lettuce and tomato; or a Hummus Wrap with zucchini, squash, roasted red peppers, spinach and hummus. Each lunch is served with Cream of Wild Rice soup, chips and dessert. Along the way, enjoy narrated highlights about the Duluth-Superior Harbor, the science and ecology of the St. Louis River system, and the area’s unique and historic bridges. Space is limited, so reserve your spot and enjoy one of the best ways to experience fall in Duluth!

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: “The Librarians” Documentary Screening
events.description: Please join the Kathryn A. Martin Library for a screening of the documentary, The Librarians, as well as a banned books discussion panel. Located in Bohannon Hall 90 on the UMD Campus. ABOUT THE FILM Librarians emerge as first responders in the fight for democracy and our First Amendment Rights. As they well know, controlling the flow of ideas means control over communities. In Texas, the Krause List targets 850 books focused on race and LGBTQIA+ stories – triggering sweeping book bans across the U.S. at an unprecedented rate. As tensions escalate, librarians connect the dots from heated school and library board meetings nationwide to lay bare the underpinnings of a large-scale coordinated extremist movement fueling the censorship efforts. Despite facing harassment, threats, and laws aimed at criminalizing their work – the librarians’ rallying cry for freedom to read is a chilling cautionary tale. Runtime: 88 min. Free

events.title: Book Signing: “Perseverance: A Memoir” by Mark Dayton
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: Join former governor Mark Dayton for a signing of his memoir Perseverance with a foreword by Hillary Rodham Clinton. In his own words, Perseverance: A Memoir details Dayton’s life story, including his childhood in a dysfunctional household, his political awakening, his early life in politics, and his friendship with Senator Paul Wellstone, whose call, “We all do better when we all do better,” served as a lodestar for Dayton’s ongoing work. The book ends with a postscript on our current moment in public life. In addition to providing an enduring record of recent political history, Dayton’s memoir offers case studies of problems being remedied swiftly under leadership motivated by empathy. Perseverance provides occasion for conversations of consequence and substance, today and for years to come. Mark Dayton served two terms as the fortieth governor of Minnesota, from 2011 to 2019. His other elected offices include state auditor and US senator. Get your copy of the book signed and meet Mark Dayton. Books will be available for purchase.

events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🚗📍 Please use the Winter Admissions parking lot/entrance and meet up with the rest of the group in the Dining Room! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.description: Relax on Lake Superior with live local music by Abe Curran, great food, and unforgettable waterfront views. Lake Superior Live is Vista Fleet’s summer music series, combining a casual harbor cruise, live performances from some of the Twin Ports’ favorite musicians, and a BBQ-style dinner. Whether you’re looking for a unique date night, a fun evening with friends, or simply an excuse to get out on the water, this cruise offers a laid-back way to enjoy Duluth’s waterfront. Weather permitting, cruises travel through both the Duluth Canal and Superior Entry, offering incredible views of Lake Superior, working waterfront activity, and the Duluth skyline. Your ticket includes a casual BBQ dinner. Grab a drink from the bar, find your favorite seat, and enjoy an evening of live music as the sun begins to set over the harbor. A full bar is available onboard with beer, wine, cocktails, soft drinks, and non-alcoholic options available for purchase.

events.title: Photography & Art at the Rock: Featuring Shawn Malone
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: September at the Rock celebrates the wonder of Lake Superior—by day, by night, and under the stars. We are proud to feature Shawn Malone, a landscape photographer and visual artist whose work has been inspired by the Lake Superior region for more than 25 years. After moving from Chicago to Marquette, Michigan, Shawn found both her home and her artistic calling along the shores of Lake Superior. Since then, she has dedicated her career to capturing the ever-changing beauty of this remarkable landscape—from rugged coastlines and dramatic weather to the brilliant colors of the aurora borealis and the quiet brilliance of the night sky. Best known for her immersive aurora and night sky photography, Shawn creates images and time-lapse films that reveal the beauty of the natural world in ways often hidden from the naked eye. Her work invites viewers to slow down, look up, and experience the wonder that unfolds after sunset. In addition to operating her Lake Superior Photo gallery in downtown Marquette, Shawn is an award-winning photographer, educator, and workshop leader. She has spent more than a decade sharing her passion for the night sky through presentations, photography workshops, and guided experiences throughout the Great Lakes region, helping others discover the magic of photographing Lake Superior under the stars. On display September 1–30. Meet the Artist: September 29 | 10 am–6 pm Experience Lake Superior through the lens of one of the region’s most accomplished night sky photographers.

You’ll be painting three trout in one painting, inspired by Jordan’s best-selling piece, “Lakeside.” She’ll walk you through the painting step by step, from blending and layering to washes and texture, while leaving plenty of room to make it your own. No watercolor experience needed. Jordan will guide you through it, and all of the supplies and instruction are included. Tickets are $52 per person, and the class will run for a little over two hours. Grab a cider, settle in, and paint some trout.

events.title: Whoopsa Daisy Farm
events.description: Come and explore the farm with your family. Jump in the corn pit, dig in the sandbox, or explore Dinoland and Fairyland. There are two playgrounds, yard games, a wagon ride through the Whimsical Woods and so much more. Feed the donkeys, goats, and chickens and walk through the berries. The farm is open to everyone Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, August 7 through October 25, 2026, from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm. We will also open Thursday, October 15 for MEA weekend from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm. Tickets are sold at the entrance in the yellow building. The cost is $8.00 a person, and infants are free. Everything on the farm is included in the price. We are off Highway 53 in Duluth at 5399 Samuelson Road.

events.title: Lunch & Leaves Cruise on the Vista Fleet
events.description: Experience fall in Duluth from the water aboard Vista Fleet’s Lunch & Leaves Cruise! Take in the beautiful fall colors of the Northland while enjoying a relaxing cruise aboard the Vista Star and a delicious lunch from MidCoast Catering. Choose from a Turkey, Bacon & Swiss sandwich with cranberry mayo, lettuce and tomato; a Ham & Provolone Croissant with lettuce and tomato; or a Hummus Wrap with zucchini, squash, roasted red peppers, spinach and hummus. Each lunch is served with Cream of Wild Rice soup, chips and dessert. Along the way, enjoy narrated highlights about the Duluth-Superior Harbor, the science and ecology of the St. Louis River system, and the area’s unique and historic bridges. Space is limited, so reserve your spot and enjoy one of the best ways to experience fall in Duluth!

Life Cycles of Iron in Art and the Landscape
events.description: 📅 Thursday, October 15, 2026 ⏰ 5:30–8:00pm 📍 MDC’s Dining Room 💲 FREE and open to all What happens when the iron beneath our feet becomes part of the art around us? Join MDC Museum & Research Center Director Allyse Freeman and painter, material researcher, and educator Elisabeth Heying for an engaging, hands-on exploration of the many life cycles of iron in art and the landscape. The evening begins with Allison MJ Collins, a representative from CHAIR, sharing how the arts are shaping the Iron Range, followed by Allyse with a brief introduction to the history and landscape of the region. Then, Elisabeth will take you on an experimental journey through the many forms and uses of iron in artmaking—from raw steel to iron oxide-based earth pigments. Watch a live demonstration of how natural minerals can be transformed into pigments and then made into paint! 🎨 Hands-on activities will include: Creating oxidation drawings on steel plates Painting with red earth pigments from the Minnesota Iron Range Exploring the connection between art, science, minerals and the landscape around us Part show-and-tell, part cooking show, part science lesson, and part art class, this unique experimental workshop invites participants to connect with the material and landscape of their home through creative experimentation. 🍴 Complimentary appetizers included! 🍹 Cash bar available! Event Schedule 5:30–6:00pm: Social hour & arrival 6:00–6:30pm: Presentations by Allison MJ Collins and Allyse Freeman 6:30–8:00pm: Experimental art workshop with Elisabeth Heying This activity is made possible by the voters of Minnesota through a grant from the Minnesota State Arts Board, thanks to a legislative appropriation from the arts and cultural heritage fund.

events.description: TICKETS Get Tickets Here Make it a group experience! Special pricing is available for groups of 10 or more: worldballetcompany.com/group-tickets. ABOUT THE SHOW The World’s MOST Iconic Ballet – With a LIVE Orchestra! The legendary tale of Swan Lake takes flight in a breathtaking production from World Ballet Company, as fate and magic entwine in a timeless battle between good and evil. Performing with a Live Orchestra, and featuring a cast of 50 international dancers, over 150 radiant hand-sewn costumes, and stunning hand-crafted sets, this spellbinding ballet captures every heart-pounding moment – from the Dance of the Little Swans to the Black Swan’s 32 fouettés, and every pirouette in between. With Tchaikovsky’s unforgettable score soaring through the air and played LIVE, immerse yourself in this mesmerizing journey where dreams, heartbreak, and hope unfold right before your eyes. Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes (including 20-minute intermission) Audience: For ages 5 & over ABOUT WORLD BALLET COMPANY World Ballet Company – Ballet Everywhere, Ballet For All. Based in Los Angeles, and led by Sasha Gorskaya and Gulya Hartwick, World Ballet Company presents the most beloved and iconic ballets of our time in cities nationwide. Driven by the belief that ballet is for everyone, performances appeal to newcomers and seasoned ballet goers alike. The company attracts many international artists and comprises renowned professional dancers representing over ten countries. To date, World Ballet Company has traveled to more than 300 cities, reaching an audience of more than 500,000 fans. WBC Website: https://worldballetcompany.com/duluth2 KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: Jaerv and OK Factor
events.description: Legendary Swedish group Jaerv and Twin Cities-based duo OK Factor return to the beautiful Sacred Heart alter stage Friday, Oct. 16. The award-winning Jaerv present an extroverted, vigorous and heartfelt folk music with influences from both jazz and pop music. The group offers a varied stage performance where five-voiced tunes blend in with energetic dances and free improvisations. Jaerv is an internationally well known act and has toured the U.S., Japan, Spain, Scotland, Ireland, Finland and Norway among other countries. Their discography includes three full length albums. New classical crossover group OK Factor was formed more than 10 years ago by cellist Olivia Diercks and violinist Karla Peters. Organic and genuine, their original compositions and arrangements feel both comfortingly familiar and uniquely fresh. The group has toured nationally, internationally and recorded five studio albums of original work. Advance E-tickets will be available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE beginning at 10 a.m Friday, Sept. 11. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). We’ll be pouring taproom-only fresh hop beer releases, brewed with freshly harvested hops to capture bright, vibrant hop flavors at their peak. Fresh Hop Beer Fresh Hop Pale Ale with Strata Hops Fresh Hop Mosaic IPA Fresh Hop Hazy IPA with Krush Hops Live Music All Day 11:00 AM–1:00 PM | Northeast Timberland Band 1:30–3:30 PM | Shorething 4:00–6:00 PM | Squid City Slingers Food Baptism River Barbecue will be serving up the goods throughout the event. It’s a fun, hands-on addition to the festival for kids, families, and animal lovers of all ages. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love. Performed by a vibrant ensemble of actors, dancers and singers, HADESTOWN is a haunting and hopeful theatrical experience that grabs you and never lets go. events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society. Sponsorship does not imply endorsement of this or any other estate/appraisal service, and museum staff members are prohibited by professional ethics from making financial appraisals.

events.description: Duluth-based Americana group Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold celebrate the release of their new album “Dedication.” Steeped in musical traditions of folk, bluegrass, country, classic rock, and blues, Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold offers a genre-blending sound that is captivating, invigorating, and sure to get your toe tapping. After two decades of writing songs and performing as a solo artist, Danny Frank released of his debut album “Smoky Gold” in 2021. He then assembled an all-star cast of seasoned musicians to fully compliment his music. “The Smoky Gold” is comprised of banjo player Harrison Olk (Tin Can Gin, Cascade Crescendo, Kind Country Band), bassist Joe Scarpellino (Smokin’ Joe, Dead Larry), and fiddle savant Erin Aldridge (Concert Master – Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra). Together the group has recorded and released the full length album “Dedication.” Opening the evening will be Adam Greuel (Horseshoes & Hand Grenades) and Kenny Leiser (Joseph Huber). events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. events.title: History Happy Hour

Discover 1920s-inspired activities and artifacts on display, enjoy music from the era, snap a photo in the billiards room, and take in a few surprises along the way. Enjoy a selection of fun, 1920s-inspired cocktails available for purchase at the cash bar before settling in for an engaging history talk by local historian Tony Dierckins. Tony will present “Drying Out Duluth: From Temperance to Prohibition,” exploring Duluth’s complicated relationship with alcohol—from the city’s early liquor ordinances and temperance movement to Prohibition and the creative ways Duluthians continued to enjoy a drink. Following the talk, enjoy dessert and a special 1920s-themed experience to round out the evening. Dress to impress and embrace the spirit of the 1920s for this one-of-a-kind night at Glensheen. events.title: Silent Film: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
events.description: The Friends of The Felgemaker invite you to experience what it was like to attend a silent movie! Renowned organist Aaron David Miller will accompany the silent film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” at 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23 on the historic Felgemaker pipe organ housed at Sacred Heart Music Center. Perfect for the Halloween season, “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” is spooky, stylish and historically significant. It is a groundbreaking German horror film which set standards for creative camera work and featured a dark and twisted style of storytelling. It is widely considered the first true horror story put to film. This masterpiece influenced later film directors such as Alfred Hitchcock and Tim Burton. Attendees are encouraged to come dressed for Halloween, adding to the film’s haunted atmosphere. Aaron David Miller returns to Sacred Heart Music Center to accompany this film on the Center’s outstanding Felgemaker pipe organ. Miller is noted for his highly imaginative and creative style, found in his performances, improvisations and compositions. He has won numerous international awards for improvisation and has given concerts and accompanied silent films across the country. Advance adult tickets are $20 (plus a $3.18 handling fee) and are available on Eventbrite HERE. Tickets will be available at the door for $20 while supply lasts. All students can pay $5 at the door. Doors at 6 pm. Show at 7.

events.description: The Research Center Presents: Ryan Vine’s The Cave: Poetry Reading & Book Signing 🗓️ Date: Thursday, October 29 ⏰ Time: 5:00-7:30pm 📍 Place: MDC’s Theater 💸 Cost: FREE On Thursday, October 29 from 5:00-7:30pm, come listen to one of Minnesota’s most celebrated modern poets—Ryan Vine! Ryan will be reading from his latest poetry collection, The Cave, which explores the topics of fatherhood, generational trauma, and the ways place and lineage connect. It has been named one of the “Best Poetry Books of 2025” by the California Review of Books and “Top 5 of 2025” by Zenith Bookstore in Duluth, MN. Ryan was born and raised on the backwaters of the St. Louis River in the Fond Du Lac neighborhood of western Duluth. Along with being a poet, he is also a professor of English at the College of St. Scholastica. His honors include the Northeastern Minnesota Book Award, the Weldon Kees Award, the Robert Watson Poetry Prize, and more. Here’s the evening’s schedule: 🥂 5:00pm: Mingling and (free!) snacks (first-come, first-served) 🗣️ 6:00pm: The poetry reading begins ✒️ 6:45pm: Ryan signs books 👋 7:30pm: We say goodnight Take a look at these reviews of The Cave: “While the poems in The Cave are thoroughly contemporary, many of their philosophical underpinnings are as old as humanity itself. Vine’s haunting meditations on fatherhood, for example, are as profound and enduring as any I’ve ever read. This is manly work, utterly masterful, and deeply moving.” — Connie Wanek “These poems are as indelible as scars—and just as full of ancient wisdom. Wonders abound: the cloud inside a dog’s eye, the way a lake holds up the sky. events.title: Neural Exercises for Autism, a conversation with the author
events.venue: At Sara’s Table Chester Creek Cafe
events.description: Is Autism an identity or a disorder, is an ongoing question which faces those who describe themselves under the umbrella of Neurodiversity language. WW Norton author, and autistic individual, Sean Inderbitzen LCSW, DSW, invites neurodiverse Duluthians to wrestle with this question with him in a small gathering setting. Themes to be covered from his new book in this talk include identity, temperment, disorder, empathy, and the role of ambiguous loss in shaping connection and rigidity. These themes like these and more appear in his new book Neural Exercises for Autism, and we invite you to meet with the author partaking in discussion, pastries, and a dive into meaning and neurodiversity. Please register for our gathering complete with readings, discussion, pastries from Sara’s Table at Chester Creek Cafe, and Alcoholic beverages available for purchase. Pastries will be provided for those who wish to partake, and beverages are guest responsibility. Our event is on a first come first serve basis. If you are unable to make it and register, please cancel as space is limited to the first 25 registrations.

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: Thursday, November 5, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment TICKETS Tickets on sale now! ABOUT 38 SPECIAL Formed in 1974, the band toured tirelessly from the start, sharpening the explosive live show that’s been 38 Special’s calling card for a half-century. Along the way, the Florida natives fine-tuned their sound too: a blend of muscle and melody, filled with the arena-rock pop hooks that would soon become staples of FM radio. Years passed... trends changed... some band members retired from the rigors... but 38 Special remained, hitting the road year after year, flying the flag for an enduring form of classic rock & roll that never dies. As 38 Special enters its sixth decade together, the music continues with Milestone. It’s the band’s first studio album in more than 20 years, and it showcases a group of road warriors with plenty of miles left in the tank. Fueled up on snarling guitars, anthemic melodies, and the desire to break new ground, they update their sound for the 2020s, bridging the gap between past and present without forgetting their rock & roll roots. “After all this time, we wanted to create a more modern 38 Special album,” says frontman and co-founder Don Barnes. “This is a fresh, updated approach to the sound we’ve been making together for so long. Why not make a big statement after all these years? When you’re reintroducing yourself to the world, ‘good enough’ doesn’t work anymore. If you’re gonna do it, you might as well go big.” Learn more at 38special.com KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

His two-decade resume includes ten critically-acclaimed albums, mentorships with iconic Hip Hop legends Chuck D and Rakim, and performances on late night shows with Jimmy Fallon and Conan O’Brien.His provocative and uplifting brand of Hip Hop has earned him coveted press features like Rolling Stone’s 40th anniversary edition and Source Magazine’s “Hip Hop Quotables”, while his outspoken social justice message has landed him on government watch lists. He’s also lectured at universities from Princeton to Stanford and delivered the keynote address at the Nobel Peace Prize Forum.When he’s not rocking the mic at Coachella or being arrested for civil disobedience in support of marginalized communities, Brother Ali travels the world learning and teaching Islamic Spirituality under some of today’s most renowned teachers. In addition to leading worship services and classes, he co-founded The Gemali Project, an organization that helps Muslim converts and spiritual seekers access the beauty of the Islamic tradition. Brother Ali recently launched The Travelers Podcast from his new home in Istanbul, exploring life’s journey with cultural, spiritual, and thought leaders from across the globe.

ABOUT THE SHOW “An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I” From Star Wars to Armageddon to Titanic to The Martian to oddly scientifically literate Beer Commercials. An entertaining and enlightening review of all the science that our favorite movies got wrong, combined with some of the stuff they got right. Incorporates recent films as well as some classics that you may not have known had any science in them at all. ABOUT NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON Neil deGrasse Tyson was born and raised in New York City where he was educated in the public schools clear through his graduation from the Bronx High School of Science. Tyson went on to earn his BA in Physics from Harvard and his PhD in Astrophysics from Columbia. In 2001, Tyson was appointed by President Bush to serve on a twelve-member commission that studied the Future of the U.S. Aerospace Industry. The final report was published in 2002 and contained recommendations (for Congress and for the major agencies of the government) that would promote a thriving future of transportation, space exploration, and national security. In 2004, Tyson was once again appointed by President Bush to serve on a nine-member commission on the Implementation of the United States Space Exploration Policy, dubbed the “Moon, Mars, and Beyond” commission. This group navigated a path by which the new space vision can become a successful part of the American agenda. And in 2006, the head of NASA appointed Tyson to serve on its prestigious Advisory Council, which guides NASA through its perennial need to fit ambitious visions into restricted budgets. In addition to dozens of professional publications, Dr. Tyson has written, and continues to write for the public. events.title: Edmund Fitzgerald: A Great Lakes Memorial
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: This annual event commemorates the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald and the total loss of the 29 crew members aboard on November 10, 1975. It is also a time to reflect on the memory of all lives lost on the Great Lakes. The lighthouse, fog signal building, and visitor center will be open for visitors. Guides will welcome visitors and provide historic site and shipwreck information. Throughout the day, visitors can watch a film about Edmund Fitzgerald in the visitor center, or join a guided tour exploring the history of Fitzgerald’s final voyage. At 4:15 pm, the lighthouse will temporarily close while the names of the crew are read to the tolling of a ship’s bell, with a rendition of the Naval Hymn. Following the ceremony, the beacon will be lit, and the tower will be open again to tour until close at 6 pm. Be sure to bring a flashlight or headlamp as the grounds and trails are unlit. The weather is unpredictable, please dress accordingly. The event will be streamed on Split Rock’s Facebook Page and the Minnesota Historical Society’s YouTube channel. Tickets are offered online and onsite. Tickets only guarantee you admission to the site and program. It does not guarantee you a parking space or specific seating at the event.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance. In his talk, Shawn uses research and case studies to show practical ways individuals and teams can surface the beliefs limiting them, reframe challenges as changeable, expand what they believe is possible and sustain those shifts under pressure. Register here for this virtual event: uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor Shawn Achor is the NYTimes bestselling author of The Happiness Advantage and The Power of Beliefs. Shawn graduated magna cum laudefrom Harvard and earned a Masters from Harvard Divinity School in Christian and Buddhist ethics. After spending 12 years at Harvard, Shawn traveled to 50 countries studying how to create an interconnected approach to potential and happiness.

events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🚗📍 Please use the Winter Admissions parking lot/entrance and meet up with the rest of the group in the Dining Room! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: The Oak Ridge Boys
events.description: Friday, November 13, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment GET TICKETS HERE ABOUT THE OAK RIDGE BOYS For more than 50 years, The Oak Ridge Boys have defined one of the most recognizable sounds in American music, blending four-part harmonies with an energetic stage presence that has earned them Grammy, CMA, ACM, and Dove Awards. With a legacy that stretches from their Gospel roots in the 1940s to their rise as Country‐Pop hitmakers, the group—Duane Allen, Joe Bonsall, William Lee Golden, and Richard Sterban—has delivered classics like Elvira, Bobbie Sue, American Made, and Thank God for Kids. Their music has produced multiple gold and platinum albums, over 30 Top Ten hits, and collaborations with icons ranging from Johnny Cash and Paul Simon to George Jones and Ray Charles. Today’s performing members are Duane Allen, William Lee Golden, Richard Sterban, and Ben James. The Oak Ridge Boys remain one of the most enduring and dynamic touring acts in the world, known for a high‐energy show that celebrates both their rich history and their continued evolution. Whether performing for presidents, recording fresh takes on their biggest hits, or exploring new musical directions with acclaimed producers, they bring the same passion that first propelled them to stardom. With decades of tradition, unmatched harmony, and a timeless catalog loved by generations, The Oak Ridge Boys continue to captivate audiences everywhere they go. Learn more at oakridgeboys.com KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: Chamber Board Member Interest
events.description: There’s a Seat at the Table. Could It Be Yours? LOOKING FOR LEADERS: Who care about business. Who care about our community. Who want to help shape what comes next. The Grand Rapids Area Chamber of Commerce is accepting applications for upcoming seats on its Board of Directors. Serving on the Chamber Board is an opportunity to bring your perspective to the table, help guide the priorities and direction of the organization, and be part of conversations that impact businesses throughout our area. Why Serve? As a Chamber Board member, you will have the opportunity to: • Help shape Chamber priorities, programs, and advocacy efforts. • Represent the perspectives and needs of our business community. • Build relationships with business and community leaders. • Contribute your experience, ideas, and perspective to the Chamber’s future. • Help strengthen the business environment in the Grand Rapids area. Who Are We Looking For? We are looking for engaged, thoughtful leaders who care about business and our community and are willing to actively participate in the work of the Chamber. Applicants must be affiliated with an active Chamber member business or organization, or hold an individual Chamber membership. We welcome applicants from different industries, backgrounds, business sizes, and areas of experience who can bring valuable perspectives to the table. What Do We Need From You? You do not need to have prior board experience or be an expert on every issue facing our business community. We are looking for Board members who are willing to: • Show up and participate in Board discussions and decisions. • Ask questions and bring your perspective to the table. • Respond to Board email inquiries, including time-sensitive votes and requests for input. • Represent the Chamber and its membership in a positive and professional way. • Participate in and volunteer at Chamber events, as you are able. events.title: A Live Conversation with Chevy Chase following a screening of National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation
events.description: Sunday, November 15, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Standing Ovations Live and Pepper Entertainment TICKETS TICKETS ON SALE NOW! ABOUT THE SHOW Pepper Entertainment and Standing Ovations Live are proud to present “A Live Conversation with Chevy Chase following a screening of National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation” at the DECC Symphony Hall. Join us for an unforgettable evening of holiday cheer and laughs as we celebrate the timeless classic, National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation, with a special screening of the film followed by a live conversation and Q&A with Chevy Chase, and his wife Jayni. Chevy and Jayni will share their behind-the-scenes stories and personal anecdotes about the making of this beloved movie that has become a Christmas tradition. But the laughter doesn’t stop there! We’ll also be taking questions from the audience, giving you the chance to have your questions answered and hear firsthand from Chevy about his storied career including SNL, Caddyshack and so much more. For those looking for an extra-special experience, a limited number of VIP tickets will be available which include a personal post-show photo opportunity with Chevy Chase himself. Don’t miss this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to have your picture taken with a true legend of comedy and film. Whether you’re a die-hard fan or simply love the holiday spirit, this event promises to be an unforgettable experience for all. Mark your calendars, grab your ugly Christmas sweater, and join us for a night of laughter and holiday cheer with National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation and Chevy Chase! ABOUT CHEVY CHASE An original member of NBC’s Saturday Night Live, Chevy Chase was the trailblazer who turned SNL success into Hollywood mega-stardom. The movies Caddyshack, National Lampoon’s Vacation, Fletch, and Three Amigos all contributed to making Chevy Chase a world-wide household name. KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society. Sponsorship does not imply endorsement of this or any other estate/appraisal service, and museum staff members are prohibited by professional ethics from making financial appraisals.

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Minnesota troubadour Mason Jennings returns performing old favorites and work from his new album “Dark Wings.” “I love song craft,” says Mason Jennings, a folksinger who has spent over two decades honing his craft both on stage and in the studio. “A song is like a boat on the water, and you’re trying to make it float with as few pieces as possible. If you do it right, a song can be very healing.” For Jennings, songwriting has always been about a personal connection, both with his audience and himself. He’s known for an unpretentious, emotive approach to folk music, combining introspective lyrics with acoustic melodies. His work has drawn comparisons to genre greats, including Nick Drake, John Fahey, and Tom Waits. But Jennings’ sound is distinctly his own, one that blends vulnerability with strength, simplicity with complexity. That style comes through on his new record: “Dark Wings.” His 18th studio album, the record finds Jennings moving between raw honesty about childhood scars, dark thoughts, spiritual questioning and a stubborn belief in the power of love. Duluth-based singer-songwriter and bandleader Breanne Marie of Breanne Marie & The Front Porch Sinners will open with a solo set. Advance E-tickets are available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). events.title: Iron Range Night
events.description: The Iron Range Rocks! Celebrate the music from Minnesota’s Iron Range with performances from The Brothers Burn Mountain, Hobo Revival and The Sectionals beginning at 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 28. Guitar and drum duo Ryan and Jesse Dermody have been performing as The Brothers Burn Mountain for 25 years. Based out of their off-the-grid, self-constructed studio near Cotton, the duo has toured relentlessly around the midwest for more than two decades. The Brothers Burn Mountain have released 11 full-length albums of original music and released a “best of” collection in 2025. Hobo Revival, based out of Nashauk, has been performing their straight-ahead brand of rock and roll across northern Minnesota for 15 years. Led by singer-songwriter Kim Nagler, the group released its latest album “The Pulled Pork Sessions” in 2024. The Sectionals are a vocal octet performing classic jazz and modern acapella favorites. The ensemble features members from throughout the Iron Range. This event is made possible in part by a grant from the Arrowhead Regional Arts Council with funds appropriated from the Minnesota Legislature from its General Fund. Advance E-tickets will be available for $20 (plus $3.18 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE beginning at 10 a.m Thursday, Oct. 1. Paper tickets will be available for $20 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). Tickets will be available at the door for $25 while supply lasts. Doors at 6. Music at 7.

events.title: Duluth Winter Village
events.description: THE MAGIC RETURNS TO HARBOR DRIVE! Dates & Times: December 5–6, 2026 | Saturday & Sunday | 10:00 am – 4:00 pm Admission & Parking: FREE to attend! (DECC Parking is $10) AN EVENT UNLIKE ANY OTHER! For one weekend only, we’re bringing together the best of Duluth in one scenic location. The 10th annual Duluth Winter Village returns along the lake on Harbor Drive this December 5 and 6 from 10:00 am – 4:00 pm. The magic of local businesses, charming wooden shopping cabins, family-friendly activities, hot food, beverages (including beer & cocktails), and carolers continues to be a magical tradition. The festivities are held outside and inside at the Duluth Entertainment Convention Center. Visitors will appreciate: Our famous holiday-themed Experiential Bar “Tinsel Tavern” — featuring cocktails from Vikre Distillery Local makers & on-site Blacksmith Soup flights On-site holiday portraits by the Christmas tree Hollybeary Kid Store is back with more shopping options for littles to pick out for their grown-ups Animals, live caroling, 25-foot lit tree Small Children and Nursing Area by Duluth Mom Duluth Winter Village merch produced by our local vendors Hug-a-Hen by the Locally Laid Egg Company Lift Bridge, freighter views and bonfires The annual event began on the grounds of Glensheen Mansion in 2016 but moved to its new location in 2021. The Duluth Winter Village is unique from other area markets in that the vendors are all local businesses with retail locations around Northern Minnesota. Participants include Bailey Builds, Altered Abode, Y-ker Acres, Hucklebeary, Frost River, the Rainbow Room, NaturaLight, The Big Lake, Wintergreen Northern Wear, Lake Superior Art Glass, Ivy Moon and the Moon Market. Food and drink from the DECC’s culinary team, Positively Third Street Bakery, Hungry Hippie Tacos, Duluth’s Best Bread, Love Creamery, Scenic 61 by New Scenic Café, TBSP Waffles, Yes Cheese, and more. For more information, visit here.

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🚗📍 Please use the Winter Admissions parking lot/entrance and meet up with the rest of the group in the Dining Room! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: Retail Employee Day
events.description: Today the City of Proctor proudly recognizes the hardworking team at Mountain Spirits Municipal Liquor Store in honor of Retail Employees’ Day. Retail Employees’ Day celebrates the dedicated people who keep stores running and ensure customers have a positive shopping experience. From helping customers find the perfect bottle, stocking shelves, managing inventory, and keeping the store welcoming and organized, retail employees play an important role in connecting products with the people who enjoy them. At Mountain Spirits, our team works year-round to provide friendly service, maintain a well-stocked store, and support this City or Proctor’s municipal enterprises. Their efforts help make shopping easy, enjoyable, and welcoming for everyone who walks through the door. Please join us in thanking the Mountain Spirits staff for their hard work, professionalism, and commitment to serving the Proctor community. Your dedication does not go unnoticed!

events.title: High Key Mondays & Industry Nights
events.description: High Key Mondays & Industry Night Are BACK! Live local music | Drink specials | 6–9pm High Key Monday is FRI-YAY for many of our industry partners — and we’re roll with it. Calling all restaurant, bar, liquor store, and brewery professionals in the Twin Ports — get on down to the Paddle for Industry Night! Show a worker ID or pay stub for $1 off all Bent Paddle beverages. Thank you for keeping our paddles in the water! Everyone is welcome! Come for the tunes, stay for the conversations, delicious beverages, and good times. This month to kick off and celebrate the return, we invite you to connect with local organizations making waves in the Twin Ports — like WE Health, Trans+ Northland, Twin Ports Artists Collective, and Men As Peacemakers. Org’s may vary based on who available each week, but the good vibes are guaranteed!

events.title: Itasca Symphony: Christmas w/The Snowman
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The Snowman is back at the Reif with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra for a second December, on its way to becoming a Grand Rapids tradition. The 1982 animated film, based on Raymond Briggs' picture book, has no dialogue. A boy builds a snowman, the snowman comes to life, and together they fly off into the night sky to "Walking in the Air." Howard Blake's music tells the whole story, and the Itasca Symphony Orchestra plays it live while the film fills the big screen. The rest of the afternoon is holiday music for the whole family. Bring the kids and the grandparents, and make it part of your December.

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.description: Minneapolis-based The Last Revel brings its exciting Americana-folk sound to the beautiful Sacred Heart altar stage at 7:30 pm Thursday, Jan. 14. Duluth-based eerie-folk quintet Superior Siren opens. Formed in 2011, The Last Revel uses traditional folk-minded three part harmonies with honest and meaningful lyrics to deliver a passionate and soul stirring performance. The group has released six full length albums and will celebrate the 10th anniversary of its landmark “Hazard & Fate” album. Their latest, “Gone For Good,” was produced by Dave Simonett of Trampled by Turtles. General admission advance E-tickets will be available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE beginning at 10 a.m Friday, Oct. 2. A limited number of front row seats will be available for $50 (plus $5.20 in fees) in advance on Eventbrite only. General admission paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). General admission tickets will be available at the door for $30 while supply lasts.

Calling all restaurant, bar, liquor store, and brewery professionals in the Twin Ports — get on down to the Paddle for Industry Night! Org’s may vary based on who available each week, but the good vibes are guaranteed!

events.title: Itasca Symphony: No Strings Detached
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Grand Rapids' own Sam Miltich joined the Hot Club of San Francisco as a teenager and has since toured internationally and played Lincoln Center. This February he brings his band home to share the Reif stage with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra: Sam on guitar, his father Matthew Miltich on bass, plus other instruments. The music travels. Choro (SHOH-roo) is the quick, bright instrumental music of Rio de Janeiro. The Nuevo Tango from Argentina. Čoček (CHO-chek) is the Romani dance music of the Balkans. And Sam got his start in the swinging guitar jazz Django Reinhardt made famous in 1930s Paris. For the finale, young string players from IOSP's programs in Grand Rapids, Bigfork, and Remer join the band and the orchestra for one big celebration of music. It's a February night out of the cold, with musicians of every age on one stage.

events.title: DSSO Masterworks 5 – In Sacred Light
events.description: A kaleidoscope of perspectives: “My Country ‘Tis of Thee”, filtered through Charles Ives’ shifting lenses. Fragments of a brilliant Schubert symphony left mysteriously unfinished. An old Lutheran hymn refracted and retold by Bach. A journey from light to darkness and back again, pieced together from a mosaic of sacred texts. Tonight’s program represents the American ideal of individual voices converging into one, unified whole. Featuring the DSSO Chorus and DSSYO Youth Symphony IVES Variations on “America” SCHUBERT Symphony No. 8, “Unfinished” BACH Cantata No. 4, Christ Lag in Todesbanden HAGENBERG Illuminare Schedule, tickets, and more info at DSSO.com

Adam has been featured on radio and television, and played some of the biggest festivals in the country, including the 2019 Woody Guthrie Festival and the 2019 Kerrville Folk Festival. The Reif Cozy Concert Series The Reif Cozy Concert Series features Minnesota-based singer-songwriters performing their own heartfelt and original compositions. You can expect a diverse range of styles, from folk and indie to blues and Americana. Each show offers a unique opportunity to connect with artists and their music in the intimate Ives Theater at The Reif Center. These poignant, stripped-down performances are sure to capture the raw intensity of the gifted storytellers grown right here in our region. events.title: Riverdance 30 – The New Generation
events.description: Sunday, March 14, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Roberts Group TICKETS Tickets on sale now! ABOUT THE SHOW Since Riverdance first emerged onto the world stage, its fusion of Irish and international dance and music has captured the hearts of millions worldwide. The Grammy award-winning music and the infectious energy of its mesmerizing choreography and breathtaking performances has left audiences in awe and established Riverdance as a global cultural sensation. To celebrate this incredible 30th year milestone, Riverdance will embark on a special anniversary tour, bringing its magic to audiences around the world. This spectacular production rejuvenates the much-loved original show with new innovative choreography and costumes and state of the art lighting, projection and motion graphics. And for the first time Riverdance welcomes “The New Generation” of performers, all of whom were not born when show began 30 years ago. John McColgan, Director of Riverdance said, “For over 30 years, Riverdance has taken us on a unique and exhilarating journey with the love and support of our audiences. The show has developed from a stage spectacle into a global cultural phenomenon. It has continuously evolved yet we ensure it always remains true to its roots. The 30th Anniversary showcases our “New Generation” of extraordinary talented performers with their electrifying energy, passion and skill in their traditions and their music and dance. Fresh, exciting and with all the magic and spectacle of the original, this is Riverdance better than ever before.” Audiences will enjoy a unique and memorable performance which blends the traditional and the contemporary, showcasing the skill and passion of the world-class of dancers, musicians and singers in the Riverdance ensemble. Composed by Bill Whelan. Produced by Moya Doherty. Directed by John McColgan. Learn more at riverdance.com KNOW BEFORE YOU GO
